summary: Return (max frequency of any vowel) + (max frequency of any consonant) in a lowercase string.
mainInsight: Count letters; keep the running maximum separately for vowels and consonants (counts only increase, so a running max is exact). Sum the two maxima.

approaches.name: Count then take two maxima
approaches.summary: Counter, then max over vowels and over consonants.

approaches.name: Running maxima during one pass
approaches.summary: Update max_v or max_c as counts grow.

promptVariants: What do you maintain per category?
Why is a running maximum valid?
options: Max vowel frequency and max consonant frequency; counts only increase
The first vowel and the first consonant seen, keeping only their indices
The sorted letters of the string, with vowels first and then consonants
The number of distinct letters in each category, summed at the end
cards.answer: Max vowel frequency and max consonant frequency; counts only increase
cards.explanation: Counts never decrease, so the maximum after each increment is the true maximum so far.

promptVariants: Why can both maxima be computed in the same pass as the counting?
What if there is no vowel or no consonant?
cards.answer: Only the letter whose count just increased can become the new maximum of its category, so comparing that count with the running maximum is enough. If a category is absent its maximum stays 0, contributing nothing to the sum.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Space complexity (26 letters): ___

cards.explanation: Vowels: a = 3 is the maximum; there is no consonant so the sum is 3. 'bbb' has consonant maximum 3 and no vowels.

incorrectOptionExplanations.7 (all letters are vowels), and 3: Not the sum of frequencies of all vowels.
incorrectOptionExplanations.1 (one distinct vowel), and 3: The first has a maximum vowel frequency of 3.
